newsitem.title: UK: BSKYB ERA TO END WITH STRONG YEAR PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: BSKYB ERA TO END WITH STRONG YEAR PROFIT.

text.p: British Sky Broadcasting Plc is expected to report 1997 pre-tax profit of at least 300 million stg as chief executive Sam Chisholm prepares to bow out, analysts said on Monday.

BSkyB, which will publish its results on Friday, is forecast to deliver pre-tax profit of 300-305 million stg, against 257.4 million stg a year ago. Earnings per share of 16.0-16.8p is forecast, up from 13.6p while BSkyB is likely to increase its dividend from 5.5p to between 6.1 and 6.5p.

The results mark the end of an era for BSkyB as Chisholm, seen as the architect of the company's rapid expansion in the 1990s, is stepping down at the end of the year on healthy grounds. His deputy David Chance, who has also suffered health problems, is also giving up his post.

BSkyB is planning a move into 200-channel digital satellite broadcasting next year, a key development which will be led by new chief executive Mark Booth. Booth, currently chief operating officer at News Corp's JSkyB satellite TV venture in Japan, takes charge on January 1, 1998.

The loss of Chisholm and Chance and BSkyB's removal at regulators' request from the Granada-Carlton BDB terrestrial digital TV venture has led to a re-rating of a stock which has long had the highest P/E multiples in the media sector.

BSkyB shares, which hit a 1997 high of 669p in February, fell as low as 420p last month. A recent rally gained pace on Monday when the shares added 14.5p to 487.5p although dealers said volume was light.

Analysts said they remained cautious about BSkyB's medium-term prospects, citing regulatory issues such as scrutiny of the way channels are packaged, higher programming and marketing costs and the investment and uncertainty associated with the launch of digital broadcasting.
They noted that BSkyB remains priced around 29-30 times current earnings and that upside was likely to remain limited until some of the above issues were clarified.
BSkyB has formed the BIB venture with, Midland Bank and Matsushita Electric Works of Japan to supply on-line services such as home shopping and home banking to digital viewers.

BIB plans to subsidise the cost of digital set-top boxes or decoders down to around 200 stg to help encourage initial take-up. But recent media reports have said that delays in obtaining European and UK regulatory approval for the subsidies could mean that BSkyB may miss its planned spring 1998 launch slot for digital satellite.
